record.original_question: Do M-matrices satisfy the Newton inequalities c_j^2 ≥ c_{j-1} c_{j+1} for all j = 1,…,n−1, where c_j is the normalized average of principal minors of order j defined by c_j = (∑_{#α=j} A[α]) / (n choose j)?

evidence.quote: 5. Newton’s inequalities. For a matrix A, let cj := ∑ #α=j A[α]/ ( n j ) , j = 0, . . . , n.
This problem has possible subproblems, e.g., 5a. Newton’s inequalities for M -matrices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be an $n\times n$ real matrix. For each subset $\alpha\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ with $|\alpha|=j$, let $A[\alpha]$ denote the principal minor of $A$ corresponding to rows and columns indexed by $\alpha$. Define
$$c_j(A):=\frac{1}{\binom{n}{j}}\sum_{|\alpha|=j} A[\alpha],\qquad j=0,1,\dots,n,$$
with $c_0(A)=1$. Recall that an $n\times n$ matrix $A$ is called an $M$-matrix if $A=sI-B$ where $B$ is an entrywise nonnegative matrix and $s\geq \rho(B)$ (the spectral radius of $B$); equivalently, $A$ has nonpositive off-diagonal entries and every principal minor of $A$ is nonnegative.

Question: Does every $n\times n$ $M$-matrix $A$ satisfy Newton's inequalities
$$c_j(A)^2 \;\geq\; c_{j-1}(A)\, c_{j+1}(A) \qquad\text{for all } j=1,2,\dots,n-1\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered affirmatively by Holtz (2005), "M-matrices satisfy Newton's inequalities" (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 133, no. 3), proving that for any M-matrix the normalized averages c_j of principal minors of order j form a log-concave sequence, i.e., c_j^2 ≥ c_{j-1} c_{j+1}.

status_evidence.title: M-matrices satisfy Newton's inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Newton's inequalities are shown to hold for the normalized coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of any (possibly singular) M-matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Holtz proved that M-matrices satisfy Newton's inequalities c_j^2 ≥ c_{j-1} c_{j+1}.

status_evidence.title: Matrices and spectra satisfying the Newton inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: When Newton inequalities hold, the averages of the k-by-k principal minors form a log-concave sequence.
status_evidence.claim: Newton inequalities for principal-minor averages correspond to log-concavity of the c_j sequence.
